parole.testo: From -uș + -ior, from Albanian -sh + Latin -olus.

Unknown. Possibly a substratum word, perhaps from a Dacian *bengas, *bongas or *bungas, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰeh₂ǵnos, with a suffix added later, akin to Albanian bung. Alternatively, a borrowing from this Albanian word.
Unknown. Possibly a substratum word, akin to Albanian burdhë (“bag, sack”). Alternatively, a borrowing from this Albanian word. Cognate of Russian бурдюк (burdjuk).
Probably borrowed from Albanian qafë, of uncertain origin. May be cognate to Ancient Greek κεφαλή (kephalḗ, “head”). Unrelated to Turkish kafa (“head”).

From older copaci (compare Aromanian cupaci, Megleno-Romanian cupaci, Istro-Romanian copaț (“thicket, brushwood”)), possibly borrowed from Albanian kopaç (“treestump”) or cognate to it as a Balkan substrate root. The current form was probably analogically formed as a singular from the earlier copaci
Probably from Albanian kurpen, kurpën, variant of kulpër.

Substratum word, akin to Albanian kurth, kurthë, or possibly borrowed from it. Alternatively from the feminine of curs, past participle of cure and curge (cf. also Medieval Latin cursa (“incursion”)).
Substratum word, akin to or derived from Albanian këpushë, or from a diminutive of cap + -ușă. Also cognate to Aromanian cãpush(ã), dialectal Bulgarian капуш (kapuš).

Substratum word, akin to Albanian katund (northern/Gheg variant katûn), or possibly derived from it. Probably of native Balkanic, possibly Illyrian origin, and ultimately Indo-European but it is a much-disputed word with numerous and varied attempted etymologies. Unknown. Possibly from a root *flutulus, or deverbative from flutura. Related to Albanian flutur, and possibly derived from it; alternatively, it may have a substratum root akin to it, or simply be of imitative origin. Compare also Aromanian flitur.
Aphetic form of sfărâmă, possibly from Albanian thërrime, or a substratum term cognate to it. Alternatively from the verb fărâma.
Akin to Aromanian guvã (“hole, cavity”), likely ultimately from Albanian guvë (“pit, cave”).

Unknown. Probably a substratum word, akin to or derived from Albanian mugull. Also, possibly from a Vulgar Latin root *muculus, diminutive of Latin mūcus, or simply reformed as a singular from mucuri as the plural of muc.

Probably derived from Albanian ujanë or from naie (“ship”) + -an. Possibly a substrate word from Thraco-Dacian.

Possibly borrowed from Albanian nepërkë (“adder, viper”), otherwise cognate to it, from fuller nepërtkë, originally ‘hatchling snake’, maybe from Proto-Slavic *nepъrtъkъ (compare Bulgarian непрътък (neprătăk, “buttercup”)). Compare Aromanian nipãrticã.

Compare Megleno-Romanian pupează. Most likely an imitative substratum word, akin to Albanian pupëzë, or possibly derived from a root pupă (now found only in Aromanian), of onomatopoetic origin, with suffix -ză. Other languages show similar forms, compare Latin upupa, Sardinian pubùsa, pupùsa, French

Might be a deverbal from Albanian shqipe, shkype, modern forms of the old term Albanian shkabë (“eagle”); which derived from Proto-Albanian *iš-gabā, from Proto-Indo-European *kobuǵos. A cognate to English hawk, Latin capys (“bird of prey”) and Russian ко́бец (kóbec, “falcon”).
Borrowed from Albanian shqipëtar.

Unknown. Possibly from archaic scrumb; a substratum word, akin to or from Albanian shkrumb. Other theories include Cuman Turkic kurum ("soot") (cf. Hungarian korom). Alternatively, it may simply be from an expressive root.
Borrowed from Albanian shpuzë, from Latin spodium.
Probably from Albanian trastë

Unknown. Possibly from Albanian vapë (“hot weather”), from Old Italian vapa (“vapor”), from Latin vapor (“heat, hot air”), though the relationship between the words is uncertain. Another theory is that it is linked to a Vulgar Latin root *vapalia, from vapa. Compare Sicilian vampa.

parole.significato: buttermilk (liquid left over after producing butter)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Albanian dhallë.
Borrowed from Albanian shpagë (“compensation, payment to end a blood feud”), from Italian paga (“payment”).
Possibly borrowed from Albanian thep (“peak, point”) or cep (“edge, tip”) or a substratum term cognate to it. Compare also Italian zeppa, inzeppare and Proto-Slavic *cĕpa.
Either from Old Albanian *abul (compare modern avull) or cognate to it as a substrate word; less likely from Latin albulus or an alteration of vapor.

Of uncertain origin: * Often considered to be a substrate word. * Other theories suggest, on the basis of what is used to make cheese, a derivation from Latin brandeum (originally meaning a linen covering, later a thin cloth for relic storage)
A substrate word, akin to Albanian brez (or possibly derived from an earlier form of it; cf. the dialectal variant form); alternatively, from Latin brandeum.
Unknown. Possibly a substrate word, perhaps from Dacian *bukas, akin to Albanian byk (or alternatively derived from it). May be linked to Polish buch.

Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic бѣлъ (bělŭ), from Proto-Slavic *bělъ (“white”). Alternatively, from Albanian balë.

Possibly borrowed from Albanian kësulë (var. kaçule). Compare Aromanian cãciulã, cãciuã, Greek κασούλα (kasoúla). Alternatively cognate to it as Balkan substratum word, or akin to Latin casula or cuculla. Other attempts have been made to link it to a Vulgar Latin *catteula, from *cattea, from cattus
Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic длато (dlato), from Proto-Slavic *dolto, or alternatively possibly from Albanian daltë.

Origin disputed. Though probably from Proto-Slavic *gotovъ. Possibly a substratum word, akin to or derived from Albanian gjemb, or alternatively from Vulgar Latin *pungulus, from Latin pungō (compare Italian pungolo) through intermediate roots *punglu > *glumpu through metathesis > *ghiumpu > ghimp(u).

parole.significato: old man, gaffer, old fogey, buzzard
parole.testo: Borrowed from Albanian gjysh, from Proto-Albanian *sūša, from earlier *sūsa. Eventually from Proto-Indo-European *suHsos, variant of *suHnús. Alternatively a substratum word, akin to Albanian gjysh.

Uncertain; possibly a substratum word, akin to Albanian grihë, or derived from Albanian gërresë (“potter's instrument for leveling”). Alternatively, from a Slavic *kresь or *gresь; compare Serbo-Croatian kresalo, kresivo (“flint, tinderbox”), kresati (“light with flint”), kresiti (“set off sparks”).

Probably a substratum word, akin to Albanian gropë, or possibly derived from it. Compare also Aromanian groapã, Bulgarian гропа (gropa). Ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *gʰrebʰ- (“to dig, scratch, scrape”). Cognate with Old Norse grǫftr (“graving, grave, burial, funeral”), Old Church Slavonic гр

parole.significato: a type of traditional peasant's or shepherd's laced sandal or moccasin worn in the country
parole.testo: Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic опинъка (opinŭka). Compare Bulgarian опинка (opinka). Probably ultimately from Albanian opingë, either directly or via Old Church Slavonic.

Origin disputed. Possibly a substrate word akin to Albanian rrëndës (“rennet”) or possibly derived from it. Compare Aromanian rãndzã. If from Albanian, from a Proto-Albanian *r̄ândə-dᶻə, which led to rrëndës.
